questions.q: Why doesn't x_acme_eqchk_equipment extend task, while x_acme_eqchk_request does?
options: ServiceNow does not allow lookup tables to extend task under any circumstances
Equipment is reference/lookup data, not a workflow record, while the request table needs task's approval and state plumbing
Both tables actually extend task, with equipment simply hiding the extra fields
equipment extends task, but request does not
questions.explain: A lookup table like equipment holds reference data pointed at by other records; the request table extends task because it needs an approval/state workflow.

Deletes the equipment_condition field from the equipment table

questions.q:
What does this ACL script actually control?

answer = gs.hasRole('x_acme_eqchk.equipment_admin') || gs.hasRole('admin');
options: Whether the current user can log into the instance at all
Whether a Business Rule is allowed to run on a table
Whether the current user may write to a specific field (equipment_condition), returning true only for equipment admins or system admins
Whether the equipment table itself exists in this scope
questions.explain: A field-level write ACL evaluates this script and assigns the result to answer; only users with the named roles get write access to that one field.

questions.q: What is the field-level consequence for a user who lacks both x_acme_eqchk.equipment_admin and admin, given the ACL above?
options: They lose all access to the entire equipment table
They can still view equipment_condition, but it's read-only to them even though other fields on the same form remain editable
They are automatically granted the equipment_admin role
The ACL has no effect unless it's also applied to the whole table
questions.explain: A field-level write ACL only restricts that one field — the rest of the form's editable fields are unaffected.

questions.q: Why is EquipmentAvailabilityChecker's Application Access set to "This application scope only" rather than "all application scopes"?
options: Nothing outside x_acme_eqchk has a legitimate reason to check equipment availability, so the narrowest access is the correct choice
"This application scope only" is the only option ServiceNow allows for class-based Script Includes
It needs to be callable from Global for the Client Script to reach it
Application Access only matters for Scripted REST APIs, not Script Includes
questions.explain: Per Chapter 5's cross-scope reasoning, Application Access should grant the narrowest reach that still lets this application's own code call it — here, scope-only is correct.
